kaps_punt: Die oudste vorms van menslike kommunikasie: Taal, simbole, liedere, kuns en dans; San-jagter-versamelaars (die eerste mense in Suider-Afrika) as 'n voorbeeld

items.bewering: Die San is verskillende groepe mense van Suider-Afrika, en hulle woon vandag nog hier. Daar woon San in Namibië, in Botswana en ook in Suid-Afrika.
items.bron: Cultural Survival (culturalsurvival.org/node/3999): most San live in Namibia and Botswana, also the northwestern Cape (South Africa), with smaller numbers in Angola, Zambia, Zimbabwe; Encyclopedia.com 'San' entry. Leaving out Angola, Zambia and Zimbabwe is incomplete, not false.

items.bewering: Hulle voorouers was van die eerste mense wat in Suider-Afrika gewoon het.
items.bron: Daily Maverick, 7 Dec 2025, on the Nature study of ancient southern African genomes (Schlebusch: the first population split is between San ancestors and all other populations; San ancestors in southern Africa for at least 10 000 years before others arrived); Gretzinger et al. 2024 (Oakhurst Rockshelter, genetic continuity through the Later Stone Age). The softened 'van die eerste' is the right form; the bare 'die eerste mense' in the CAPS label would be too strong, and the lesson body does not use it.

items.bewering: Die San het van jag en veldkos geleef. Daarom noem ons hulle jagter-versamelaars.
items.bron: South African History Online, 'San hunter-gatherers' (sahistory.org.za/node/65069): food from hunting wild animals and gathering plant foods such as fruits, nuts, berries and roots.

items.bewering: Hulle het nomadies geleef en agter water en kos aan getrek.
items.bron: South African History Online, 'San hunter-gatherers': they did not settle in one place and moved to find different plant foods at different times of the year and good water resources.

items.bewering: Hulle het geen skrif gehad nie, en tog het hulle elke dag gekommunikeer.
items.bron: South African History Online, 'Oral tradition and indigenous knowledge' (sahistory.org.za/article/oral-tradition-and-indigenous-knowledge): San knowledge passed on orally by elders. The Bleek and Lloyd archive (UCT) exists because 19th-century |Xam narratives had to be written down by outsiders.

items.bewering: Party San jag en versamel vandag nog, maar die meeste leef anders.
items.bron: Cultural Survival (culturalsurvival.org/node/3999): only a few San, mainly those still living in the desert, follow the traditional way of life; most are much less nomadic and many work for wages or live in poverty.

items.bewering: Die San se tale dra klanke wat in min ander tale voorkom. Ons noem dit klikklanke, want jy maak dit met 'n klik van jou tong.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Click consonant': clicks occur in all three Khoisan families of southern Africa; outside them only in Hadza and Sandawe (Tanzania), in neighbouring Bantu languages that borrowed them (e.g. Xhosa, Zulu), and in Dahalo; about 24-38 living languages in total. 'Min ander tale' holds. Clicks are made with the tongue against the roof of the mouth; even the rare bilabial click needs a tongue closure at the back.

items.bewering: Met taal vertel die San vandag nog stories vir mekaar. Ouers het hulle kennis met woorde oorgedra, en niks daarvan was neergeskryf nie.
items.bron: South African History Online, 'Oral tradition and indigenous knowledge': in the San tradition, people learnt what their elders told them, passed from one generation to the next.

items.bewering: Die San het skyfies uit volstruiseierdop geslyp en dit aan halssnoere geryg.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Ostrich eggshell beads': fragments are broken from the shell, perforated, trimmed and ground on a coarse surface, and strung on cord. The lesson leaves out the drilling, which is a simplification, not a falsehood.

items.bewering: San-vroue maak vandag nog sulke krale.
items.bron: Horniman Museum object record HC.1999.989: beads made by women of the San people in Botswana; Cultural Survival (culturalsurvival.org/node/10749): San still make ostrich-eggshell beads today, now with shell from ostrich farms; Wikipedia 'Ostrich eggshell beads': ethnographic data show women made them.

items.bewering: Mense het die krale as geskenke aan mekaar gegee. So het party krale honderde kilometers ver van hand tot hand gegaan.
items.bron: Stewart et al. 2020, PNAS (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7104358): strontium isotopes show ostrich-eggshell beads in highland Lesotho came from several hundred kilometres away, through exchange networks like hxaro, the Ju/'hoan gift exchange first documented by Polly Wiessner (University of Toronto news release; Wikipedia 'Ostrich eggshell beads': beads could travel several hundred kilometres).

items.bewering: Die halssnoer het dus sonder woorde gewys aan wie jy verbind is. So 'n teken wat vir iets anders staan, noem ons 'n simbool.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Ostrich eggshell beads': the beads cement and reassert friendship ties and advertise these bonds outwardly; the variation in them carries social information. So the bead stands for a relationship, which fits the lesson's own definition of 'simbool' (Britannica and Collins: something that represents or stands for something else). The bead-as-symbol mapping holds.

items.bewering: Die San sing wanneer die groep bymekaarkom. Sang is een van die maniere waarop hulle stories en kennis aan mekaar oordra. 'n Storie in 'n lied kan van ouma tot kleinkind voortleef.
items.bron: Nelson Mandela University news, 'Reintroducing songs in the |Xam language' (de Villiers and du Plessis): songs were built into |Xam stories recorded by Bleek and Lloyd; Wikipedia 'San healing practices' (Katz): the group gathers for the dance and the women sing the n/um songs; SAHO 'Oral tradition': stories passed from elders to children. The claim is modest ('een van die maniere', 'kan') and the sources carry it. Note that the |Xam songs Bleek and Lloyd recorded have not been performed since 1879, so the lesson must not later be widened to say that particular songs have survived.

items.bewering: Die San het met verf op groot rotse en teen grotmure geskilder, en ons noem dit rotskuns.
items.bron: Bradshaw Foundation, 'San Rock Art of the Drakensberg'; Metropolitan Museum essay 'San ethnography' (paintings on rock surfaces in shelters, some eland painted with blood). Most painted sites are rock shelters rather than deep caves, but 'grotmure' is a fair word for a Grade 4 learner.

items.bewering: Op die klip sien jy groot diere soos elande en ook seremonies.
items.bron: Metropolitan Museum essay 'San ethnography': eland especially important and widely painted; Wikipedia 'David Lewis-Williams' / Bradshaw Foundation: eland is the animal painted most often in many regions; AllAfrica, 'Dance Scenes in South African Rock Art' (Feb 2026): dance and ritual scenes in rock art in KwaZulu-Natal, the Free State and the Eastern and Western Cape.

items.bewering: Navorsers dink baie skilderye het met die San se geloof en hulle danse te doen gehad.
items.bron: Metropolitan Museum essay 'San ethnography': as scholars understood San beliefs, much of the art was linked to the healing or trance dance; Wikipedia 'David Lewis-Williams'. 'Navorsers dink' is the right level of confidence, because interpreting old art from 20th-century ethnography is methodologically debated.

items.bewering: Vandag is die rotskuns 'n bron wat vir ons van die San se lewe vertel. So leer ons oor mense wat lank gelede self niks neergeskryf het nie.
items.bron: Metropolitan Museum essay 'San ethnography' (rock art read together with San ethnography to understand beliefs and ritual); Bradshaw Foundation.

items.bewering: By 'n spesiale dans sit die vroue in 'n kring om die vuur, sing en klap. Meestal dans die mans in 'n ry om daardie kring.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'San healing practices', citing Elizabeth Marshall Thomas: women sat in a circle around a fire and sang, men danced single file around the fire; Smithsonian Folkways liner notes FW04316: men dance around the singing women, sometimes joined by women. 'Meestal' is right: a second type with shamans in the centre is also recorded (Metropolitan Museum essay).

items.bewering: Dit is die vroue se sang wat die dans aan die gang hou.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'San healing practices', citing Richard Katz: the women's singing of the n/um songs helps 'awaken' the n/um and the healer's heart so healing can begin.

items.bewering: Sommige mans en vroue raak in 'n spesiale toestand, en ons noem hulle sjamane. Hulle probeer siek mense gesond maak.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'San healing practices': by adulthood about half the men and a third of the women have become healers, who enter !kia and remove sickness; Metropolitan Museum essay: older women and men act as shamans in the dance.

items.bewering: So sê die dans vir die hele groep dat hulle saam vir hulle siek mense sorg. Die dans is dus 'n manier om te kommunikeer, nie net 'n gewoonte nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'San healing practices': the dance is a communal event, and healers also mend social conflicts as well as removing sickness. This is an interpretation, but a supported one.

items.bewering: Al vyf hierdie maniere is vandag nog by ons. Jy praat elke dag, en jy sien simbole op paaie. Mense sing nog, maak nog kuns en dans nog.
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary 'symbol': a letter, character or picture used in place of a word, which covers road-sign pictograms. The comparison of then and now holds: speech, symbols, song, art and dance are the same kinds of communication, and the lesson does not claim the forms themselves are unchanged.

items.bewering: Die San sing vandag nog, hulle dans nog en hulle maak nog krale.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Kuru Dance and Music Festival' and Music in Africa 'Kuru San Dance Festival': San dance groups from Botswana and Namibia perform hunting, courtship and trance healing dances and songs at D'Kar, held yearly since 1997; Horniman Museum HC.1999.989 for beads.

items.bewering: Nie een van die vyf het weggeval nie, en masjiene het net daarby gekom.
items.bron: Follows from the sources in the two items above: all five forms (speech, symbols, song, art, dance) are documented as still practised. This is an absolute claim about kinds of communication, not about any particular language or song, and at that level it holds.

items.bewering: kommunikasie: Om 'n boodskap aan iemand anders oor te dra.
items.bron: Vocabulary.com 'communication': giving information or ideas to someone through words, actions or sounds.

items.bewering: San: Groepe mense wat vandag nog in Suider-Afrika woon. Hulle eie tale dra klikklanke. Hulle voorouers het van jag en veldkos geleef, nie van vee nie.
items.bron: Cultural Survival (culturalsurvival.org/node/3999); Wikipedia 'Click consonant' (clicks in all three Khoisan families, so every San heritage language has them); SAHO 'San hunter-gatherers'. 'Hulle eie tale' is accurately worded, since many San today also or only speak other languages.

items.bewering: jagter-versamelaars: Mense wat van jag en veldkos leef. Hulle plant nie kos nie en hou nie vee nie.
items.bron: SAHO 'San hunter-gatherers': food from hunting wild animals and gathering wild plant foods, as opposed to farming or herding.

items.bewering: nomadies: Om van plek tot plek te trek sonder 'n vaste huis.
items.bron: SAHO 'San hunter-gatherers': did not settle in one place and moved with the seasons.

items.bewering: kraal: 'n Klein stukkie met 'n gaatjie deur, wat jy aan 'n draad ryg.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Ostrich eggshell beads': perforated bead blanks strung together on a cord.

items.bewering: simbool: Iets wat vir iets anders staan, soos 'n teken of 'n woord.
items.bron: Collins (via dictionary search): something that represents or stands for something else; Britannica Dictionary 'symbol': also a letter, character or picture used in place of a word.

items.bewering: rotskuns: Kuns wat mense op klip verf of in die klip inkap.
items.bron: Bradshaw Foundation 'San Rock Art'; Metropolitan Museum essay 'San ethnography': southern African rock art includes both paintings and engravings.

items.bewering: sjamaan: Iemand wat in 'n spesiale toestand raak, die geesteswêreld bereik en die groep help.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'San healing practices': healers enter !kia, perceive and remove sickness, mend social conflicts and make spiritual journeys; Wikipedia 'David Lewis-Williams' (shamans describe a journey to the spirit world).

items.bewering: klikklanke: Klanke wat jy met 'n klik van jou tong maak en waarmee jy woorde bou.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Click consonant': clicks are consonants, ordinary speech sounds used to build words, and in Khoisan languages they may be the most common consonants.

opsomming: All 33 claims check out, including every superlative and quantifier ('van die eerste', 'min ander tale', 'die meeste', 'meestal', 'nie een'), and the bead-as-symbol and then-and-now comparisons hold; the lesson body correctly softens CAPS's 'die eerste mense' to 'van die eerste mense', and that softening should not be undone.
